title: Drilling of a Leased Safe Deposit Box for Unpaid Rent, and the Holding of Its Contents
content:
Where rent on Safe Deposit Boxes remains unpaid 120 days after the rent due date, the drilling notice is sent by certified mail to the address on file and the rental becomes pending drilling.

## The notice period before the box may be opened

The box may be drilled only after 30 calendar days have passed since the drilling notice was mailed.

Calendar days are counted with the day after the date the notice was mailed as day 1. Drilling is allowed when the current date is on or after the notice date plus 30 days. The notice date is the one recorded against that rental when the certified notice was mailed, and it is that record, read for the rental in question, that fixes the day the count runs from.

## The opening itself

Drilling is done under dual control with a witness. The contents are inventoried and sealed, the drilling charge set for that size is made as a service charge on the rental, and the lease ends.

## The contents afterwards

The contents are held for 12 months. Within that period they may be retrieved by the former lessee on paying everything due together with the charge for retrieving contents held after a drilling. After that period they are reported to the state unclaimed property program, which lies outside this basis.

## Cure

Paying everything due before the drilling date returns the rental to active.

## The notice period at its boundary

Suppose, on hypothetical dates, that the certified notice is mailed on 6 June. The day after it, 7 June, is day 1, and the thirtieth day is therefore 6 July.

| Hypothetical date | Position in the count | Whether the box may be drilled |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 July | day 29 | no |
| 6 July | day 30, the notice date plus 30 days | yes |
| 7 July | beyond day 30 | yes |

The boundary is inclusive: the thirtieth day is itself a day on which the box may be opened.
